An excellent snapshot of authentic Japanese cuisine in Vietnam.
Feb 2025 • Friends
From the Yucatan of the female attendants to the Japanese greetings to the extensive menu and drinks selection all the way down to the presentation, this restaurant is a fine example of how to really give the customer a small piece of culture from another country.

The menu is large and has plenty of options available from sashimi plates to the casual Katsudon bowl, there'll be something on the menu for even the fussiest of eaters. The drinks menu was also brilliantly presented with a wide range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages with Sake and Japanese beer alike.

The food portion sizes were a little small but to be honest, it's the same portion size you'd get in Japan, so well presented. The sashimi was delicate and tasteful, an amazing representation of Japan. We also got the wagyu tataki, tempura plate, salmon skin salad and grilled fish. Nothing bad can be said as we were all smiles and our taste buds were having a feast.

Prices aren't cheap and you'll be looking to spend around the $100 USD mark for dinner if you go with at least 3 or 4 people so budget accordingly. This isn't your run of the mill Vietnamese restaurant.

Overall, for the price you pay you get twice more with the service, menu and taste. Definitely worth a visit if you want a small break from Vietnamese cuisine.
